Chapter 10: The Practice of Everyday Wonder
Imagine a barista, hustling through the morning rush. In the middle of making coffee, she starts to wonder—where do these beans come from?
Curious, she asks her suppliers, digs into stories about coffee farmers, and experiments with new ways to brew. Suddenly, her daily routine isn’t just a job—it’s a source of pride, a connection to people and places far away, and even a little spark of joy.
Or think about a parent, walking their child to school. They stop for a moment, noticing the leaves turning red. “Why do they change color?” the child asks.
The parent isn’t sure, so together, they look it up. They marvel at the science behind it, but also the beauty.
What could’ve been just another walk becomes an adventure—a chance to see the world through fresh eyes.
Let’s be honest, most of us rush through our days, checking off tasks and racing against deadlines. It’s easy to get caught up in the routine.
But here’s something to pay attention to: the folks who make space for wonder—who pause, ask questions, and really notice what’s around them—they discover a life that’s so much richer. The world’s packed with mysteries, just waiting to be explored.
The best part? Practicing curiosity doesn’t require fancy tools or training. All it takes is a willingness to be present, to really pay attention, and to ask yourself, “What’s interesting here?”
It’s about being open to surprise, delight, and the idea that there’s always something new to learn—even in the most ordinary moments.
Over time, this habit transforms how you see yourself, how you relate to others, and how you move through the world. It brings resilience when things are uncertain, sparks creativity when you’re stuck, and adds joy to the everyday.
Remember, curiosity isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about living with questions, embracing what you don’t know, and finding meaning in the search itself.
It’s a practice anyone can choose—every single day.
